extracted.intended_audience: interested parties in the antidumping duty administrative review (respondents, exporters, importers, counsel, and other trade stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for participation in the Department of Commerce's antidumping duty administrative review (preliminary results), including deadlines, filing content and format, calculation methodology references, assessment and cash-deposit rules, and instructions to Customs and Border Protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission-by-withdrawal rule (19 CFR 351.213(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce will rescind an administrative review, in whole or in part, if the party or parties that requested a review withdraw the request within 90 days of the publication of the notice of initiation of the requested review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests for administrative review that were timely withdrawn result in rescission for those companies; the notice rescinds the review with respect to seven of eight companies in accordance with 19 CFR 351.213(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology statutory citations for price/value calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce is conducting this administrative review in accordance with section 751(a)(2) of the Act and has calculated export prices in accordance with section 772(a) of the Act; constructed export prices in accordance with section 772(b); and normal value in accordance with section 773 of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a full description of the methodology underlying Commerce's conclusions, see the Preliminary Decision Memorandum available via ACCESS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of calculations (19 CFR 351.224(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce intends to disclose to interested parties the calculations performed for these preliminary results within five days after public announcement of the preliminary results, or if there is no public announcement, within five days of the publication of these preliminary results in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of the agency's calculations is time-limited to five days after announcement/publication to allow parties to prepare case briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case brief and rebuttal brief filing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties may submit case briefs no later than 30 days after the date of publication of these preliminary results of review. Rebuttal briefs, limited to issues raised in the case briefs, may be filed no later than five days after the date for filing case briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are strict and govern the window for raising and responding to issues in the review record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief content requirements: table of contents and table of authorities (19 CFR 351.309(c)(2) and (d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties who submit case briefs or rebuttal briefs in this proceeding must submit: (1) a table of contents listing each issue; and (2) a table of authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These formatting/content elements are required for briefs submitted to Commerce in this proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public executive summary requirement and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce requests that interested parties provide, at the beginning of their briefs, a public executive summary for each issue raised in their briefs and limit each public executive summary to no more than 450 words, not including citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce will use the public executive summaries as the basis of the comment summaries included in the issues and decision memorandum accompanying the final results. Parties should include footnotes for relevant citations in each public executive summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing request procedure and contents (19 CFR 351.310(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested parties who wish to request a hearing must submit a written request to the Assistant Secretary for Enforcement and Compliance, filed electronically via ACCESS. An electronically filed document must be received successfully in its entirety by Commerce's electronic records system, ACCESS, by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time within 30 days after the date of publication of this notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should contain: (1) the party's name, address and telephone number; (2) the number of participants; and (3) a list of issues to be discussed. Issues raised in the hearing will be limited to those raised in the respective case briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on rebuttal briefs' scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal briefs are limited to issues raised in the case briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebuttal briefs cannot raise new issues; they may respond only to arguments actually presented in case briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment-rate calculation for individually examined respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: For any individually examined respondents whose weighted-average dumping margin is above de minimis (i.e., greater than or equal to 0.5 percent) in the final results of this review, Commerce will calculate importer-specific ad valorem duty assessment rates based on the ratio of the total amount of antidumping duties calculated for the examined sales to the total entered value of the examined sales to that importer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes how Commerce translates an examined-sales-based margin into an importer-specific ad valorem assessment rate for liquidation/assessment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of entries where respondent did not know merchandise destined for US
rubrics_metrics.description: For entries of subject merchandise during the POR produced by each respondent for which it did not know its merchandise was destined for the United States, Commerce will instruct CBP to liquidate such entries at the all-others rate if there is no rate for the intermediate company(ies) involved in the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an intermediate company has no assigned rate, use the all-others rate for liquidation of such entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero or de minimis margin liquidation instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the individually-selected respondent's weighted-average dumping margin is zero or de minimis, or an importer-specific assessment rate is zero or de minimis, Commerce will instruct CBP to liquidate the appropriate entries without regard to antidumping duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The de minimis threshold is 0.5 percent; margins/rates below that result in liquidation without AD duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment instructions for rescinded companies (19 CFR 351.212(c)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For companies for which Commerce is rescinding this review, Commerce will instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on all appropriate entries at a rate equal to the cash deposit of estimated antidumping duties required at the time of entry, or withdrawal from warehouse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce intends to issue these rescission instructions to CBP no earlier than 35 days after the date of publication of this notice in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of assessment/liquidation instructions and stay when CIT summons filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce intends to issue assessment instructions to CBP no earlier than 35 days after the date of publication of the final results of this review. If a timely summons is filed at the U.S. Court of International Trade, the assessment instructions will direct CBP not to liquidate relevant entries until the time for parties to file a request for a statutory injunction has expired (i.e., within 90 days of publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This controls the timing of liquidation/assessment to account for litigation and statutory injunction opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash deposit requirements upon publication of final results (section 751(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon publication of the notice of final results, the following cash deposit requirements will be effective for all shipments entered on or after the date of publication: (1) cash deposit rate for companies listed in the final results equals the weighted-average dumping margin established in the final results; (2) for merchandise exported by producers/exporters not covered in this review but covered in a prior segment, the cash deposit rate will continue to be the company-specific rate published for the most recently completed segment of this proceeding in which they were reviewed; (3) if the exporter is not a firm covered in this review, a prior review, or the original investigation but the producer is, then the cash deposit rate will be the rate established for the most recently completed segment for the producer; (4) the cash deposit rate for all other producers/exporters will continue to be 2.02 percent, the all-others rate established in the less-than-fair-value investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cash deposit requirements, when imposed, shall remain in effect until further notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final results timeline (section 751(a)(3)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise extended, Commerce intends to issue the final results of this administrative review, which will include the results of its analysis of issues raised in any briefs, within 120 days of publication of these preliminary results of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard 120-day target for completing an administrative review's final results after preliminary results publication, subject to statutory authority to extend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importer reimbursement certificate requirement (19 CFR 351.402(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Importers have a responsibility under 19 CFR 351.402(f)(2) to file a certificate regarding the reimbursement of antidumping duties prior to liquidation of the relevant entries during this POR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply could result in Commerce's presumption that reimbursement of antidumping duties occurred and the subsequent assessment of double antidumping duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Preliminary Decision Memorandum and supporting materials (ACCESS requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Preliminary Decision Memorandum is a public document on file electronically via Enforcement and Compliance's Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Centralized Electronic Service System (ACCESS), which is available to registered users at https://access.trade.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must be registered in ACCESS to view the complete decision memorandum and underlying calculations and corroborating materials referenced by Commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to comment on preliminary results
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce preliminarily finds the estimated weighted-average dumping margin and invites interested parties to comment on these preliminary results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice establishes the record and procedural windows (briefs, rebuttals, hearings) for parties to contest, support, or otherwise comment on preliminary findings.
